# CBDB-Desktop: Office (Look At Office) label revisions, 2026-10-28

Eighth form in the review of HTML labels against the MS Access FormLabels table (form code LAO, 39 rows in the updated 643-row table). Changes are in the Office form's index.html only; no back-end change was needed. The page script was syntax-checked, and the page was loaded in a scripted browser (jsdom): all 41 labels written by setLanguage were compared with their translations in all three languages, and the OFF-1 checkbox behaviour was checked, with no script errors. **Not yet tested in the running app**; spacing and fit are still to be checked. A copy of the file before these changes was kept as index.before-labels.html. Revised later the same day with the user's answers: "Look At …" in titles, 任官記錄 for the postings tab, LAO 37–38 dormant, and the Export Options heading removed. This report also records a change to the shared stylesheet (CSS-2), prompted by Networks.

## How to revert a label

All labels are in the translations object near the top of the script, under english, traditional and simplified. Change the value of the key in the **Key** column, in the language concerned. Each line has a comment naming its FormLabels row (or "No row") and, where changed, the earlier wording. Where the English changed, the same text is also written in the HTML element; setLanguage('english') overwrites it on load.

Many labels on this form were fixed bilingual text in the markup ("Office 官职", "Type 类型", "Place 地点"), so the Chinese never followed the language buttons, and in traditional mode showed simplified characters. Those labels now have ids and keys. Where setLanguage already overwrote a bilingual markup text (the headings, Select Place, the tabs), the markup now has the English alone.

## Notes

**LBL-91.** "CBDB: " + form name, as decided on 2026-10-28. The English form name is the HTML's own, "Look At Office". The Chinese was 官职查询 ("office query"), in simplified characters in every mode. It is now 查看職官 / 查看职官, with 查看 as on the other forms and 職官, the term for Office(s) in BIO 53 and LAG 11. The English names had varied between forms ("Look At Entry" and "Look At Office", but "Looking at Kinship" and "Looking at Social Networks"); on 2026-10-28 the user chose "Look At …" for all, and Kinship and Networks were changed to match.

**LBL-92.** As on the other forms: id="lnkNavigation", a navigation key, and '← ' + t.navigation in setLanguage.

**LBL-93.** Select Office and All Offices take LAO 4 and 15 (選擇官名, 所有官名), replacing 選擇官職 and 所有官職. The heading and the Office label have no row; they now use 官名 too, so the section uses one word. The Type label is LAO 3, with 類别 corrected to 類別.

**LBL-94. Address sections.** The two place buttons, "Place People 地点人物" and "Place Offices 官职地点", become **Select Place** (LAO 20, 21, 選擇地名); the section heading above each says which address it is. All Places is 所有地名 (LAO 16, 17). LAO 26 and 27 are "Include Subordinate Units (Office)" and "(People)", 含下轄行政區(官) / (人); the (官) / (人) is left out because each checkbox is inside its own headed section. The Place labels and the Office Address heading have no row: Place is 地名, as in SF_ADDR 16, and Office Address is 官地址, the term LAG 16 uses for an office's address (Office (Offices) 職官 (官地址)). People Address keeps 人物地址. **Check the width:** each checkbox row now holds Include Subordinate Units and Use XY References side by side, both much longer than before.

**LBL-95. Date filter.** The four radio buttons take LAO 33, 34, 39 and 35: No Dates, Use Index Years, **Use Office Years** (利用任官年份) and Use Dynasties. The traditional and simplified "Index Years" option had read 生卒年 ("birth and death years"), which is a different thing from index years; it now reads 利用指數年. From / To are 始年 / 終年 (LAO 1, 2). No colons were added: the labels sit inline between the two year boxes, as before. The To labels had a fixed width of 24px, too narrow for 終年; it is now a minimum width. The Select Dynasties button showed the HTML's "Select Dynasties" only until the page loaded, after which setLanguage replaced it with "Choose" (pick key). It now has a selectDynasties key (選擇朝代, as on Entry and Networks).

**LBL-96. Actions and exports.** Run Query takes LAO 5's English (the button read "Query") and gets the ▶ of the other forms. The four GIS / KML buttons were "GIS Offices", "KML Offices" and so on. They now follow LAO 6 and 7: Save Offices to GIS (保存官名于GIS), Save People to GIS (保存人名于GIS), and, with no rows of their own, Save Offices to KML and Save People to KML on the same pattern. "Neo4j" becomes Save to Neo4j (LAO 36). Store Person IDs follows the regional-usage rule. Export Query Results had 導出 in traditional and now has 匯出. The **Export Options** heading was removed, with its exportOptions key and setLanguage line: it sat below the export buttons with nothing under it, and was the heading of the Access form's encoding radio buttons (ASCII, UTF-8 …), which are gone now that every export is UTF-8 (user, 2026-10-28).

**LBL-97. Tabs.** LAO 10 gives 官名 ("office names") for the postings tab. That describes the tab poorly, since it lists postings, so the user chose **任官記錄 / 任官记录** (2026-10-28), replacing 官職記錄. LAO 11 gives 人名 for the People tab, which was used, and its English "People in Office" replaces "People". LAO 10's English, "Offices Postings", looks like a slip for the HTML's "Office Postings", which was kept.

**Comment.** The comment above translations points to this report.

## OFF-1: Sub-units and Use XY enabled only with a place selected

**Change.** In each address section, Include Subordinate Units and Use XY References now start disabled. They are enabled when the address picker returns a place for that section, and unticked and disabled again by that section's All Places button, through a new helper, setAddrOptionsEnabled(target, enabled). Before, both pairs were always enabled, and a box ticked with no place selected (or left ticked after clearing the place) was still sent with the query (peopleAddrSubUnits, officeAddrUseXY and so on). This matches Entry (ENT-1), Associations, Status and Texts.

**Markup.** As on Entry: the ids moved from inner &lt;span&gt;s to the &lt;label for=…&gt;s, so the global disabled-label rule greys the text, and chk-sep is now on a &lt;span&gt; wrapping the Use XY checkbox and its label.

**jsdom check.** On load all four boxes are disabled. Picking a people place enables only the people pair; picking an office place enables the office pair and leaves ticked people boxes as they are; All Places on each section unticks and disables only its own pair.

## CSS-2: Labels of disabled number boxes greyed (all forms)

**Request.** On Networks, the labels of the kinship limits (Max Ancestor Generations etc.) stayed black while their boxes were disabled. The user asked for this to be a general rule in the stylesheet.

**Cause.** cbdb_styles.css has one disabled-label rule (CSS-1), input[type="checkbox"]:disabled + label, which greys a label that **follows** its checkbox. A number box's label comes **before** the box (&lt;label for="txt-max-up"&gt;Max Ancestor Generations:&lt;/label&gt; &lt;input type="number" id="txt-max-up"&gt;), and CSS has no "previous sibling" selector, so CSS-1 can't reach it.

**Change.** A second rule, directly after CSS-1:

```css

label:has(+ input[type="number"]:disabled) {

color:  #aaa;

cursor: default;

}

```

It greys any &lt;label&gt; immediately followed by a disabled number box, on every page. :has() is supported by Chrome and Edge 105+, Safari 15.4+ and Firefox 121+. In an older browser the rule is ignored and the labels simply stay black, as before. A copy of the stylesheet before the change was kept as cbdb_styles.before.css.

**Check.** With the stylesheet loaded into the Networks and Kinship pages in jsdom, the rule matched all four kinship-limit labels on each page when their boxes were disabled (computed colour #aaa) and none when they were enabled.

**Where it applies now.** Networks (the four kinship limits, disabled until Use Kinship Parameters is ticked) and Kinship (the four step limits, disabled while Mourning Circle is ticked). Other forms pick it up automatically if they disable a number box whose label comes immediately before it. Text boxes are not covered, since none is disabled with a label before it at present; the selector can be widened to input:disabled if that changes.

## Issues

1. **Untranslated text.** The placeholders ((none selected), 中文, (none), year), the Type-box texts built from the office picker's search ((Search), (Search all), (All dynasties), with fixed Chinese), the address-picker labels ([All Filtered], [Multi-select]), "No results yet…", and the status and error messages are English only or fixed in one language.
1. **Results-table headers.** Hard-coded and mixed, as on the other query forms (Name / 名, Index Yr, Office / 官名, Appt, Office X …).
